difficultyReason: Single causal claim with one obvious alternative. The stimulus attributes a sales increase solely to menu expansion, and the correct answer introduces a confounding event.
stimulus: A restaurant owner reports that after expanding the menu to include vegetarian options, the establishment's revenue increased by 20% over the following quarter. The owner concludes that adding vegetarian dishes was the primary driver of the increased revenue.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the owner's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Vegetarian dishes are more expensive to prepare than meat-based dishes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The restaurant hired three new servers in the same quarter that the menu was expanded.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Other restaurants in the area also began offering vegetarian options during this period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The restaurant's vegetarian customers spend the same amount per meal as non-vegetarian customers.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vegetarian dishes now make up only 15% of the restaurant's total menu items.

explanations.correct: Hiring new servers in the same quarter as the menu expansion provides an alternative explanation for the revenue increase. The owner attributes growth to the menu alone, but improved staffing could have increased service quality and customer capacity, thereby driving revenue growth independently of the vegetarian options.
explanations.A: Irrelevant to whether the menu expansion caused the revenue increase; cost of preparation does not explain the rise in overall revenue.
explanations.C: Other restaurants offering vegetarian options does not explain why this particular restaurant's revenue grew; if anything, it might suggest competition, but doesn't weaken the causal claim about the owner's own expansion.
explanations.D: Supports the relevance of the vegetarian addition; if vegetarian customers spend equally, they contribute proportionally to revenue growth.
explanations.E: Irrelevant; the question is not whether vegetarian options dominate the menu, but whether their addition caused revenue growth.

difficultyReason: Simple causal claim in a medical context. The stimulus links a drug dosage increase to symptom improvement; the correct answer introduces timing or alternative causation.
stimulus: A pharmaceutical company conducted a study in which patients taking a pain reliever at the recommended dosage reported an average pain reduction of 30%. When the dosage was increased by 50%, patients reported an average pain reduction of 50%. The company claims that the increased dosage is the cause of the improved pain relief.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the pharmaceutical company's claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Patients in the higher-dosage group were aware that they were receiving a larger dose.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The study lasted six months, which is a sufficient timeframe for a drug's effects to stabilize.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pain relievers at all dosages interact negatively with certain other medications.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The higher-dosage group began the study one month after their initial pain episodes, whereas the standard-dosage group was enrolled immediately after symptoms onset.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The higher dosage is associated with mild gastrointestinal side effects in some patients.

explanations.correct: If the higher-dosage group started the study one month after symptom onset, their pain may have naturally diminished over that month before the study began. This timing difference provides an alternative explanation for the observed improvement in pain reduction and undermines the claim that dosage alone caused the better outcome.
explanations.A: Strengthens the causal claim; awareness that they received a higher dose is not evidence that the dose itself didn't work — it could even reinforce the effect through placebo, but the effect is still real.
explanations.B: Irrelevant to whether dosage caused the improvement; establishing a stable timeframe doesn't address competing explanations.
explanations.C: Irrelevant; drug interactions don't explain why one dosage works better than another in the same population.
explanations.E: Irrelevant to the causal mechanism; side effects do not address whether increased dosage improves pain relief.

difficultyReason: Single causal claim in an economic context. The stimulus links a tax cut to business expansion; the correct answer offers a confounding factor.
stimulus: After the city council enacted a 15% property tax reduction for businesses, commercial expansion in the downtown district increased significantly over the next year. City officials attribute this expansion directly to the tax cut, arguing that lower taxes freed up capital for reinvestment.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the officials' argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The 15% property tax reduction applies only to businesses that expanded their facilities.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A major technology corporation announced plans to relocate its regional headquarters to the downtown district three months before the tax cut was enacted.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Previous tax reductions in the city have had minimal impact on commercial expansion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Many businesses in the downtown district report that the tax reduction was welcomed but not decisive in their expansion decisions.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The commercial expansion rate in surrounding municipalities remained flat during the same year.

explanations.correct: If the technology corporation announced its relocation before the tax cut was enacted, the expansion was likely already planned and anticipated. This provides an alternative explanation for the observed commercial growth, independent of the tax reduction. The expansion would have occurred even without the tax cut.
explanations.A: Irrelevant; whether the tax cut applied before or after expansion does not address whether it caused the expansion.
explanations.C: Weakens by undermining the general causal link, but doesn't directly contradict the officials' specific claim about this expansion.
explanations.D: While businesses say the tax cut wasn't decisive, this is a weak weakener because 'welcome but not decisive' is ambiguous and doesn't rule out that it contributed.
explanations.E: Strengthens the claim; if surrounding areas stayed flat while the downtown expanded, the tax cut appears more influential.

difficultyReason: Single causal claim about student performance. The stimulus attributes test score gains to a new teaching method; the correct answer introduces an alternative cause.
stimulus: A school district implemented a new reading curriculum focused on phonetic instruction. In the year following implementation, standardized reading test scores for third-grade students increased by an average of 12 percentile points. The superintendent concludes that the new curriculum is responsible for the improved test performance.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the superintendent's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The increase in test scores was consistent across all demographic groups in the district.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Third-grade teachers received extensive professional development and coaching specific to the new curriculum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Phonetic instruction is based on decades of educational research supporting its effectiveness.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the same year the new curriculum was adopted, the district also reduced class sizes from 25 to 20 students.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Several other districts that adopted the same curriculum also saw increased reading test scores.

explanations.correct: Reducing class size from 25 to 20 is a significant confounding variable. Smaller class sizes are known to improve academic outcomes independently, so the 12-percentile-point gain may result from the smaller classes rather than the new curriculum itself.
explanations.A: Strengthens by showing the effect was robust and not limited to one group; consistency actually supports the causal claim.
explanations.B: Strengthens; teacher training supports the idea that the curriculum was properly implemented and thus caused the gains.
explanations.C: Strengthens by lending credibility to the curriculum's causal potential.
explanations.E: Strengthens by providing corroborating evidence across multiple districts.

difficultyReason: Simple causal claim about environmental policy. The stimulus links a pesticide ban to bird population recovery; the correct answer offers a competing explanation.
stimulus: An environmental agency banned the use of a pesticide known to harm bird populations. Two years after the ban took effect, the population of songbirds in the region increased by 40%. The agency attributes this increase directly to the pesticide ban.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the agency's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The songbird population had been declining steadily for the previous decade before the ban.

choices.label: B
choices.text: During the same two-year period, several new wildlife preserves were established in the region, providing additional habitat for songbirds.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The pesticide was widely used by agricultural operations throughout the region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Songbird populations in regions where the pesticide was still legal remained stable during the same period.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The pesticide had been banned in other regions with similar results.

explanations.correct: The establishment of new wildlife preserves provides an alternative explanation for the 40% population increase. Increased habitat alone could drive population growth, independent of or in addition to the pesticide ban. This undermines the agency's claim that the ban was the direct cause.
explanations.A: Strengthens by confirming that conditions improved after the ban; prior decline makes the recovery more attributable to the ban.
explanations.C: Supports the causal claim; widespread use makes the ban's impact more plausible.
explanations.D: Strengthens by showing a contrast; regions without the ban saw no increase, suggesting the ban caused the increase in the region studied.
explanations.E: Strengthens by providing corroborating evidence in other regions.

difficultyReason: Single causal claim about technology adoption. The stimulus links a software update to productivity gains; the correct answer introduces a temporal confound.
stimulus: A company rolled out a new software system designed to streamline workflow. In the three months following the rollout, employee productivity increased by 18% on average. Management concludes that the new software is responsible for the productivity improvement.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens management's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The company provides regular training to employees on new software systems.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Three months after the software rollout, the company also implemented a new performance bonus system tied to productivity metrics.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The software system had been thoroughly tested before rollout and was found to be reliable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Different departments experienced similar productivity gains despite using the software in different ways.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The software required employees to change their established work processes.

explanations.correct: If a performance bonus system was also implemented at the same time, this provides an alternative explanation for the productivity increase. Employees may have worked harder due to the incentive structure rather than because of the software's efficiency.
explanations.A: Strengthens by suggesting the software was properly adopted and thus more likely to drive gains.
explanations.C: Strengthens; reliability supports the idea that the software functioned as intended and caused the gains.
explanations.D: Strengthens by showing consistent results across departments; this supports the causal link.
explanations.E: Irrelevant; requiring process change does not explain whether the software caused productivity gains.

difficultyReason: Single causal claim about legal policy. The stimulus links a stricter enforcement policy to crime reduction; the correct answer offers an alternative explanation.
stimulus: A police department implemented a strict enforcement policy targeting minor infractions such as traffic violations and disorderly conduct. Within one year, reported felony crimes in the jurisdiction decreased by 25%. Department officials attribute this decline to the deterrent effect of strict enforcement.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the officials' argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Police officers conducting traffic stops reported that they were more aware of criminal activity in their jurisdiction.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the same year the strict enforcement policy was implemented, unemployment in the jurisdiction decreased by 12%.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The strict enforcement policy required training of officers to recognize patterns associated with serious crimes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other jurisdictions that adopted similar strict enforcement policies also reported reductions in felony crimes.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Crime prevention advocates had long argued that strict enforcement of minor infractions would reduce serious crimes.

explanations.correct: If unemployment decreased by 12% in the same year, this provides an alternative explanation for the crime reduction. Improved economic conditions and employment are known to reduce crime independently of enforcement policies. The crime decrease may result from economic improvement rather than the strict enforcement policy.
explanations.A: Strengthens by suggesting officers gained the ability to detect crime through the increased enforcement activity.
explanations.C: Strengthens by supporting the idea that the policy was implemented with the intent and capability to reduce serious crimes.
explanations.D: Strengthens by providing corroborating evidence across multiple jurisdictions.
explanations.E: Strengthens by providing expert support for the causal claim; advocates predicted this outcome.

difficultyReason: Single causal claim about medical intervention. The stimulus links a new exercise regimen to weight loss; the correct answer introduces a confounding change.
stimulus: A fitness clinic introduced a new high-intensity interval training regimen. Participants in the program lost an average of 18 pounds over eight weeks. The clinic's director concludes that the intensity and design of the new training regimen is the primary cause of this weight loss.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the director's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: High-intensity interval training is known to burn more calories per unit of time than moderate-intensity continuous exercise.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Participants in the program were also required to follow a structured low-calorie meal plan provided by the clinic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The clinic's facility was upgraded with new exercise equipment concurrent with the introduction of the training regimen.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Participants reported high satisfaction with the training program and indicated they intended to continue exercising.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most participants had not engaged in regular exercise for at least two years prior to enrolling in the program.

explanations.correct: If participants followed a structured low-calorie meal plan simultaneously with the exercise regimen, dietary change provides an alternative explanation for the weight loss. The 18-pound loss may result from calorie restriction rather than the training regimen's intensity and design.
explanations.A: Strengthens by supporting that the high-intensity approach is physiologically effective for calorie burning.
explanations.C: Irrelevant; new equipment does not provide an alternative explanation for weight loss, though it might support the claim.
explanations.D: Irrelevant to causation; participant satisfaction does not explain what caused the weight loss.
explanations.E: Strengthens by suggesting participants were deconditioned and thus more likely to benefit from a new training stimulus.

difficultyReason: Single causal claim about historical event. The stimulus links a new marketing campaign to sales growth; the correct answer introduces a market-wide confound.
stimulus: A beverage company launched an aggressive marketing campaign featuring celebrity endorsements. In the following quarter, the company's sales increased by 35%. The marketing director attributes this growth to the campaign's persuasive power and the appeal of the celebrity endorsers.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the marketing director's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The celebrity chosen for the campaign had a large and loyal fan base.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Industry-wide beverage sales increased by 30% during the same quarter due to favorable weather and increased outdoor consumption.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The company's television advertisements were aired during prime-time slots with high viewership ratings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Competitors did not launch similarly high-profile marketing campaigns during the same period.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The beverage company had previously used celebrity endorsements without achieving significant sales growth.

explanations.correct: If the entire beverage industry experienced a 30% sales increase in the same quarter, this provides an alternative explanation for the company's 35% increase. The growth may be attributable to favorable market conditions (weather, outdoor consumption) rather than the marketing campaign. The campaign's impact is unclear when industry-wide growth is accounted for.
explanations.A: Strengthens by explaining why the celebrity endorsement would have been persuasive.
explanations.C: Strengthens by supporting the campaign's reach and persuasive potential.
explanations.D: Strengthens by suggesting the company had a competitive advertising advantage.
explanations.E: Weakens but is not the best answer; it attacks past performance but doesn't directly explain the current increase.

difficultyReason: Single causal claim about language acquisition. The stimulus links a language immersion program to student proficiency; the correct answer introduces a selection bias.
stimulus: A school district implemented a new language immersion program in which all instruction in mathematics and science is conducted in Spanish. After one year, students in the immersion program scored 22 percentage points higher on Spanish proficiency assessments than students in the traditional program. The superintendent concludes that the immersion approach is responsible for this superior proficiency.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the superintendent's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students in the immersion program reported greater confidence in their ability to communicate in Spanish.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The immersion program requires students to complete an entrance assessment, and only students with prior Spanish language exposure were admitted.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The immersion program employed native Spanish speakers as teachers in the mathematics and science courses.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Research on language immersion has consistently demonstrated its effectiveness across multiple studies and school contexts.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Teachers in both programs used interactive, student-centered instructional techniques.

explanations.correct: If only students with prior Spanish language exposure were admitted to the immersion program, the higher proficiency scores may result from the students' pre-existing language background rather than the immersion approach itself. This selection bias undermines the causal claim that the program design caused the improvement.
explanations.A: Supports the efficacy of the program; greater confidence correlates with the program's potential effectiveness.
explanations.C: Strengthens by supporting the quality of instruction in the program.
explanations.D: Strengthens by providing external evidence for the immersion method's effectiveness.
explanations.E: Irrelevant; both programs using the same teaching techniques doesn't explain the performance difference.
